hook_text: Nine friends average 20 minutes of reading. One bookworm walks in — and suddenly the 'average' describes nobody. Here's why.
clip_script: The pool: the newcomer tips more than two hours in. The pool jumps from 180 to 310 minutes, and split among ten people that is 31 minutes each. But glance around the room: nine of the ten actually read LESS than 31 minutes. The split now describes almost nobody — one enormous contribution has distorted it. That is what an outlier does to a mean: the mean is fair to the TOTAL, not to the people. The queue: the newcomer walks quietly to the very back, and every other person keeps their exact place. The middle of ten people falls between the fifth and sixth — between 19 and 22 — so the median is 20,5. Barely a flicker.
visual_style: Animated pool of glowing minutes overflowing as a giant contribution splashes in, the 'mean' marker dragged upward past nine unimpressed stick figures, then a calm ordered queue where the middle marker holds still.
pacing: Fast splash and jump-cut to the distorted mean, dramatic pause on nine-out-of-ten below it, calm slow shot of the unmoved queue, punchline on the word median.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to master mean, median and mode.
